defects: The desktop presentation remains close to the dated reference, with thin section rules, underlined navigation and little hierarchy beyond heading size.
Mobile timetable entries repeat six vertically stacked fields for every session; the 6000px capture reaches only Friday, with prices still much farther down.
The small, tightly packed uppercase mobile navigation is poorly suited to older members using the site poolside.
The captured mobile notice shows only part of the closure announcement rather than a readable set of notices.
K6.note: It retains the club faithfully and fixes the reference's fixed-width phone layout, but leaves the dated presentation and makes checking a full week unnecessarily laborious.

defects: The mobile navigation extends beyond the right edge, clipping the Contact link.
Large introductory sections precede the timetable, and displaying the entire week as mobile cards pushes prices below the 6000px capture.
The desktop layout spends substantial space on introductory material before showing the information returning members mainly need.
M9.note: Clearer typography and useful timetable and price shortcuts improve the original, but clipped phone navigation and a very long default schedule undermine the refresh.

defects: The mobile timetable expands all 27 sessions into long cards, with the 6000px capture reaching only the start of Sunday and not the prices.
No day-selection controls are visible above the long timetable, making a particular day's sessions harder to isolate.
The desktop first viewport is largely introduction and decoration, with actual timetable rows below the fold.
The captured closure notice is only partially visible rather than presented as a fully readable announcement.
Q2.note: This is a faithful, more readable version of the old site, but the exhaustive mobile timetable and weak task prioritization keep it short of a convincing modern refresh.

defects: The mobile navigation clips the Contact link at the right edge.
The hero, four notices and welcome section all precede the timetable, delaying the primary returning-member task.
The prominent hero actions emphasize sessions and joining without an equally direct price shortcut.
The desktop join panel leaves a large unused area beneath the small illustration beside the narrow form.
Q7.note: Readable notices, clear day controls and consistent club styling make a strong refresh, though phone navigation overflow and an introduction-heavy hierarchy need attention.

defects: The default all-week mobile timetable is extremely long; the 6000px capture reaches only Saturday, leaving the price section out of view.
Later day controls extend outside the initially visible mobile tab strip without a strong visual cue that more days are available.
Repeated lane, level and coach metadata gives each mobile session considerable height.
The desktop news content occupies only part of its available width, leaving an unnecessarily empty area alongside it.
S3.note: A clear, recognizable and well-organized refresh with useful navigation, held back mainly by the excessive length of its default mobile timetable.

defects: The desktop layout remains very close to the reference, with limited improvement in hierarchy or visual polish.
The mobile layout places the complete week's timetable before membership, requiring a long scroll before prices appear near the capture's bottom.
The mobile header hides section navigation behind Menu, while the hero provides no prominent task shortcuts.
The captured mobile notice displays only part of its message.
S5.note: A cautious, content-preserving repair that improves readability and phone fitting but offers little beyond a competent basic restyling.

defects: The hero and welcome section still precede the timetable, giving introductory material priority over returning members' main task.
The mobile header navigation wraps into a small, crowded multi-line arrangement.
Later days are outside the initially visible mobile day-control strip.
The desktop join section has a narrow form and substantial unused space below its accompanying illustration.
U3.note: A coherent and readable club-preserving refresh whose focused daily timetable works well, although the phone header and information order could be sharper.

defects: The mobile hero emphasizes sessions and joining, while prices remain behind the membership navigation rather than receiving their own quick action.
Four vertically stacked membership cards add considerable mobile scrolling despite containing relatively little information.
The desktop join layout leaves a conspicuous unused area beside the form beneath the small illustration.
U6.note: The strongest practical refresh puts the timetable ahead of the welcome material, makes day controls and session cards readable on phones, and preserves the familiar club identity.

defects: The welcome illustration and copy still sit ahead of the timetable, adding scrolling before the main member task.
The mobile Menu hides the section links instead of leaving timetable and prices directly visible in the header.
The reduced header logo makes the club name relatively small.
Small secondary session details and news dates are less comfortable for older members than the main body text.
W5.note: A balanced, readable and faithful refresh with a manageable daily timetable, but its mobile navigation and introduction-first ordering could serve regular members better.

defects: The mobile header navigation wraps awkwardly, leaving Contact on its own line.
The complete week remains expanded on phones, pushing membership prices close to the bottom of the 6000px capture.
Compact secondary timetable text is harder to scan than the bold times and session names.
The hero prioritizes timetable and joining rather than offering an equally prominent price shortcut.
Y2.note: A sensible and recognizable improvement with relatively compact session groups, though the long mobile week and awkward header stop it feeling fully resolved.

defects: The full week's mobile session cards consume almost the entire 6000px capture, with prices still below the visible schedule.

The lengthy welcome section appears before the timetable despite members mainly needing times and prices.
Y3.note: The recognizable palette and stronger typography help, but the mobile page devotes too much space and emphasis to introductions and joining rather than quick member lookup.

defects: Mobile sessions use tall, repeated label-and-value lists; the 6000px capture reaches only Saturday and never shows membership prices.
